 Judgment
1. This appeal arises from LAR No.2/2015 which was disposed of by the Reference Court as per a common judgment along with six other LARs.
Section 4(1) Notification under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is dated 11.02.1982.
The extent of land acquired involved in the present L.A.R is 5.16 Ares.
Land Acquisition Office awarded compensation fixing land value at the rate of Rs.2,545/- per Are for 3.46 Ares and Rs.636/- per Are for 0.50 Ares.

2. When the Reference Court answered the reference in LAR No.10/2005, the claimants filed an application under Section 28A seeking fixation of land value in accordance with the land value fixed in LAR No.10/2005.

The District Collector redetermined the land value at Rs.5,728/- for Rs.2,545/-
and Rs.1,431/- for Rs.636.
On reference, the Reference Court redetermined and fixed the land value at the uniform rate of Rs.6,000/- for the entire extent of acquired land.

When the matter was taken for consideration, the learned Senior Government Pleader Sri. Rekha C. Nair confirmed that as against the judgments in LAR No.49/2014 & 9/2016 which were disposed of as per the said common judgment, on the basis of the legal opinion the Government has not opted to file appeal before this Court and the same has become final.
In the said cases also the land value was fixed at the uniform rate of Rs.6,000/- per Are.
The same is binding in this case.
Hence, there is nothing to interfere with the land value fixed by the Reference Court.

sentences.text: Another contention is that the entire land acquired from the claimants was not taken into possession and certain extent was treated as permitted stand.

It is seen from the impugned order that though the respondent contended that a part of the property acquired from the claimants is treated as permitted stand, the Reference Court refused to accept the said contention and held that the respondent has no right to deduct any acquired land towards the permitted stand.
It is seen that LA.APP. NO. 305 OF 2019 2025:KER:40781 no evidence was adduced in this regard by the respondent before the Reference Court.
Hence, the respondent has no right to exclude a part of the acquired property as permitted stand.
Hence, there is nothing to interfere with the judgment passed by the Reference Court which is impugned in this Appeal.
5. Accordingly, the Appeal is dismissed.

Sd/-
